```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

`publish()` sends results to a named destination. This project's
`settings.yml` defines one folder destination, `local-site`, which is a
gitignored folder in the project (a relative `path:` starts at the project
root), and makes it the default. Each publish adds
a versioned bundle with an offline reader page and a SHA-256 manifest. Run
notebooks 02 and 05 first: this one publishes what 05 saved.

```{r}
settings("publish")
```

To start from an empty site, remove what earlier runs published.

```{r}
unlink("local-site", recursive = TRUE)
```

## Publishing R objects

A data frame becomes a table with every row and a profile of each column.
`slug` names the folder; `title` is what the site index shows.

```{r}
bp_long <- data_read("inputs.final.bp_long")
sbp_by_visit <- data_read("outputs/tables/sbp_by_visit.csv")

publish(sbp_by_visit, slug = "sbp-by-visit", title = "Mean systolic pressure by arm and visit")
```

A fitted model becomes coefficients, standard errors, 95% intervals, and fit
statistics. The observations stay behind.

```{r}
bp_model <- readRDS("outputs/models/sbp_mixed_model.rds")
publish(bp_model, slug = "sbp-mixed-model", title = "Mixed model of systolic pressure",
        description = "Random intercept per participant; visit by arm interaction.")
```

A hypothesis test becomes a test summary. This compares the change from first
to last visit between arms.

```{r}
last_visit_change <- bp_long |>
  group_by(participant_id, treatment) |>
  filter(visit_number == max(visit_number), visit_number > 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # A missing reading at the last visit leaves no change to compare
  filter(!is.na(systolic_change))

change_test <- t.test(systolic_change ~ treatment, data = last_visit_change)
change_test
publish(change_test, slug = "sbp-change-ttest", title = "Change in systolic pressure, first to last visit")
```

A ggplot becomes an SVG figure.

```{r}
change_plot <- ggplot(last_visit_change, aes(treatment, systolic_change)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change in systolic pressure (mmHg)")
publish(change_plot, slug = "sbp-change-boxplot", title = "Change in systolic pressure by arm")
```

## Publishing files

A saved file publishes as is.

```{r}
publish("outputs/figures/sbp_trajectory.png", title = "Systolic pressure trajectory")
```

Publishing the same slug again adds a version. Look for `v/1` and `v/2` in the
folder listing further down.

```{r}
publish(sbp_by_visit, slug = "sbp-by-visit", title = "Mean systolic pressure by arm and visit (rerun)")
```

## Publishing a notebook

`publish_notebook()` renders a Quarto document and publishes the HTML. This
renders `docs/bp-summary.qmd`, so it takes a few seconds. The title comes from
the document's YAML (`title:`); pass `title` or `description` to override.

```{r}
publish_notebook("docs/bp-summary.qmd", slug = "bp-summary")
```

## What's on the site

The site index lists every artifact. Open `local-site/index.html` in a
browser, then click through to the reader pages.

```{r}
site_index <- jsonlite::read_json("local-site/index.json")
vapply(site_index$artifacts, function(a) paste0(a$slug, " (v", a$version, "): ", a$title), "")
```

Each artifact folder holds the files, an `artifact.json` manifest, and `v/`
with every version.

```{r}
list.files("local-site/sbp-by-visit", recursive = TRUE)
```

## publish_data(), publish_dir(), and publish_list()

These follow `publish.default` too, and take `to` to pick another
destination. `publish_data()` writes a data frame in the format you ask for
(CSV, RDS, Parquet, or JSON) without the table reader that `publish()` adds;
the name of `dest` becomes the slug.

```{r}
publish_data(sbp_by_visit, "sbp_by_visit_data.parquet", format = "parquet")
```

`publish_dir()` publishes a whole folder as one artifact.

```{r}
publish_dir("outputs/figures", dest = "all-figures")
```

`publish_list()` lists what's at the destination, with sizes, times, and the
local reader page for each artifact.

```{r}
publish_list()
```

## Framework Cloud and GitHub Pages (not run)

These need a Framework Cloud login or a project token in `.env`, which this
offline project doesn't have. `cloud_status()` is safe to run and shows the
connection state.

```{r}
cloud_status()
```

The rest are shown but not run:

- `cloud_login()` and `cloud_logout()` connect this machine to Framework
  Cloud.
- `publish(..., to = "cloud")` publishes to Cloud, where `visibility`,
  `password`, and `collection` work. On a folder destination they stop with
  an error before anything is written.
- `publish(..., to = "github")` commits and pushes a bundle to the project's
  GitHub Pages site.
- `ledger_list()` and `ledger_push()` read and push the project's data hash
  ledger on Cloud; `data_save()` pushes quietly when a project token exists.
- `cloud_sync()` and `cloud_settings()` sync your global settings with Cloud.
- `skills_sync()` and `structure_import()` send skills and folder layouts to
  your Cloud account.
- `storage_test()` checks S3 credentials.

```{r}
#| eval: false
cloud_login()
publish(bp_model, to = "cloud", slug = "sbp-mixed-model", visibility = "public")
publish("outputs/notebooks/bp-summary.html", to = "github", slug = "bp-summary")
ledger_list("inputs.final.bp_long")
ledger_push()
cloud_sync()
storage_test()
```

Without a token, the ledger functions stop with a clear message.

```{r}
#| error: true
ledger_list()
```

A Cloud-only option on a folder destination fails before delivery.

```{r}
#| error: true
publish(sbp_by_visit, slug = "sbp-by-visit", password = "secret")
```
